oliver: Heads-up — enabling FP8 kernel on L40S for atlas-13b canary produced a small but consistent token-level drift. Repro steps + quick notes below.

oliver: Repro (local canary):
- model: redwood/atlas-13b:fp8-hybrid
- env: RUN_KERNEL_FP8=1 KERNEL_MODE=hybrid CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
- eval: eval-suite-v2 (generation/qa/paraphrase)
- observed: perplexity +0.6%, top-1 token shift ~0.9%, occasional fallback to q8 path

maria: Hmm, similar pattern we saw on H100 last quarter — activation saturation in middle layers caused small logit skew. Do you have logs/snippets?

oliver: Pasted small excerpt of logits/probs (sanitized):
```
layer19: max_act 14.2 clip_warn=0
layer21: max_act 27.8 clip_warn=1
layer22: token_prob_spike at step 34 -> topk shift
```
Also saw kernel emitting fallback events: `FALLBACK_Q8: layer=22 reason=scale_overflow`.

devin: Try per-channel scaling flags — FP8_SCALE_PER_CHANNEL=1 and FP8_CLIP=0 as a quick experiment. Per-channel scaling fixed a similar skew for us.

oliver: Will run that. Quick perf/quality numbers from current canary: latency ~18ms/token (was 21), throughput +12%, quality delta (perplexity) +0.6% worse. Not catastrophic but measurable on eval set.

canary-bot: Canary deploy 4512346775 -> 4512346820: 18 nodes, 15 healthy, 3 in fallback.

maria: -0.6% perplexity is material. If fallback triggers, we need to know whether entire request used fallback or only specific layers. Also check WARMUP_KV granularity — warmup tokens change KV-statistics and can hide drift.

devin: Also run AWQ vs GPTQ modes. Set FP8_QUANT_MODE=awq and then =gptq. AWQ preserved logits better for long-prefix tests in our internal bench.

oliver: Noted. Adding WARMUP_KV=32 and running AWQ/GPTQ comparison.

sara: To structure triage: 1) small bisect enabling layers (kernel_mask) to find first layer that flips distribution; 2) collect per-layer activation histograms and scale factors; 3) AWQ vs GPTQ comparison; 4) stress long-prefix (2k tokens) and short context separately.

oliver: I'll start bisect now (kernel_mask approach) and upload histograms. If bisect reproduces, we can add a temporary routing rule to keep atlas-13b on q8 on L40S until we fix.

maria: Also try FP8_AUTOSCALE=0 to force static scales — that will tell us if autoscaling logic is the culprit.

devin: If you get a reproducible layer, I can try a microkernel patch to add guard-bands for accumulation or reduce accumulation stride. Could unblock rollout quickly.

oliver: Thanks. I'll post results in this thread. tagging @sara for rollout guard decisions. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: Note: canary log bundle available at https://canary.redwood/internal/4512346789 (requires corp vpn).
